Synopsis:
    The Fed's Inspector General released a report calling for reforms to how regional Fed bank presidents and senior staff are selected. Key issues flagged: Class C directors (appointed by the Board of Governors) lack adequate financial conflict-of-interest screening and disclosure requirements. Additionally, the Board has failed to formally document the candidate selection process across Reserve Banks, leading to inconsistent practices. The Board concurred with the IG's recommendations and committed to corrective actions. No monetary policy stance is discussed.
